newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Enterprise has base for growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Enterprise has base for growth.

text.p: Exploration and production firm Enterprise Oil Plc on Thursday sang the praises of its high quality and low risk assets, which would enable the firm to consistently repeat its solid performance in the last two years.

New chief executive Pierre Jungels said Enterprise had an advantage over many rivals in that it was not plagued by political unrest or major environmental headaches in the countries where it is operating.
The company also had the benefit of being only slightly involved in natural gas, where persistent oversupply has depressed prices, Jungels said.

"Enterprise has a high quality asset base bacause in comparison to a lot of competitors we are mostly in oil and in safe countries," Jungels said after Enterprise earlier reported a 40 percent increase in 1996 profits.
"Secondly, our asset base can grow strongly over the next few years," Jungels told Reuters in an interview.
A former British Gas executive, Jungels in January took over the helm from Graham Hearne, who now solely acts as chairman.
Enterprise is active in Britain, Denmark, Italy and Norway, while it is also working hard to make the Gulf of Mexico a new core area.
Britain's largest exploration and production company earlier raised its output estimate for 1999 to 320,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from a previous forecast of 300,000.
Jungels said recent discoveries in the UK were the main reason for Enterprise to expect a higher output, after production rose three percent to 242,932 in 1996.
The combination of good assets and highly skilled staff is "the guarantee that we can reproduce the performance of the past two years on a consistent basis," Jungels said.
He forecast that further engineering work in Italy was giving Enterprise increased confidence that production and reserves could be raised there in due time.
Meanwhile, he said the seismic looked good for the Gulf of Mexico, which he expected could be put in production relatively quickly as facilities were nearby.
